title: Meet the 7 Women Who Have Been Selected for Both the Songwriters Hall of Fame & Nashville Songwriters Hall of Fame
summary: Taylor Swift & her frequent collaborator Liz Rose are in both halls, along with five other top female songwriters.
contentText:
When Taylor Swift is inducted into the Nashville Songwriters Hall of Fame this fall, it will be the second institutional honor for her songwriting this year. She was inducted into the New York-based Songwriters Hall of Fame in June.

Swift, 36, is the youngest inductee in the history of the Nashville Songwriters Hall of Fame. She was the second-youngest inductee in the history of the Songwriters Hall of Fame; Stevie Wonder was just 32 when he was honored in 1983. (The two organizations are not related in any way, though they have common aims.)

Related

Taylor Swift to Be Inducted Into Nashville Songwriters Hall of Fame: ‘I Wanted to Learn With & From the Best’

Swift released a gracious statement on Tuesday when news broke that she will be among the 2026 inductees into the Nashville Songwriters Hall of Fame: “From the time I started writing songs as a child, I fixated on Nashville as the perfect place to be. I wanted to learn with and from the best and get to immerse myself in a community of storytellers, and thankfully, Nashville turned out to be exactly what I’d dreamed of – a town that validated and prioritized hard work, determination and imagination. Where the writers show up to work every day even when the mysterious muses and the magic don’t. To be honored by this city I love so much is a beautiful thing, and I’m very grateful.”

Swift will be the 42nd individual to be inducted into both of these Halls of Fame; and just the seventh woman.

Let’s take a closer look at the seven women who have been recognized as great songwriters by both organizations. They are listed in chronological order by the date they received their second induction.
